newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's sees one-third foreign ownership.
newsitem.headline: Foster's sees one-third foreign ownership.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd on Thursday said it expected foreign investors to account for roughly a third of its share register after its capital reconstruction.

Chief executive Ted Kunkel said that it had an agreement, however, that any one investor would only be able to buy a stake equal to a maximum of five percent of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's shareholding in the company under changes to the share register announced earlier on Thursday.

Under the reconstruction, Foster's will buy back almost all of Japanese brewer Asahi Breweries Ltd's 13.8 percent stake while 86 percent of a 36.5 percent stake held by BHP will be sold widely through institutions.
Kunkel said he expected the shares to be sold in a matter of days.
At the end of the sell-down, Foster's expected foreign shareholders would own about one-third of the company, within government restrictions on offshore ownership of stock.
"We are an international company today. We have operations in North America, Europe, Asia, Australia and I think that (level of foreign ownership) is about right," he told Reuters.
"A good international spread is desirable, equally a good retail spread in Australia is desirable," he said.
Foster's had no problems with North American brewers Miller and Molson Cos taking a stake in Foster's.
Foster's has a 40 percent stake in Molson Breweries, with the Canadian parent occasionally mooted as a potential buyer of the Australian firm.
